items.title: 68191_William (Bill) H. Challis Oral History Interview
items.q: We had guys to sing, and Frankie was in front of the band... Frankie was a nice guy, real nice guy.

ctx.x: Right, somebody to make the announcements, somebody to sing, somebody to do something. We had guys to sing, and Frankie was in front of the band, but it wasn't the same thing. You could tell when he was up there, he was just standing up, where with Whiteman there's so much presence there that these are my boys, that sort of thing. You don't get that with the other guys. But anyway, the people gather around then he turns around and talks to them. "What do you want to hear?" Well, I can almost tell in his mind what…

And they started off playing it in such a corny way, (Sings), they started going like that until they realized there's Paul up there and let's not make a fool out of him because actually it was his decision. He made "St. Louis Blues" and this is something we never played. Then they played it and you know, it was faked mostly, and they played it very well.
